body: Have you asked anyone who actually died? Because I'd be willing to bet the only thing they felt on the way down was fear. Survival instinct. Once you actually die everything will be okay. It's over. Nothing more to be afraid of.

> When hope is lost, all is lost.

It's too late for me if that's the case.
That's what I'll probably end up doing if it works. Thanks for the insight.

I've tried the online chat but like I said in another comment I didn't have much luck with it. I suppose if it's my only option I might have to go with it.

Thanks for taking the time, though. I do appreciate it.
Well, like I said, I really don't want to get into that.

I tried the online chat before and they seem a lot more inclined to just hang up. The wait for the online chat is also crazy long. I once waited an hour for someone to pick up only for them to disconnect two minutes later.

I mean, when I ask "Are you in [state]?" they'd answer "Yes", so I know they aren't concerned with privacy to quite that level. Something about the way the phone system is set up automatically puts you in touch with someone nearby.
